beats.prompt: Choose an espionage goal and decide which organization or location the party will investigate over several missions.
Give characters outside the Spy career useful support roles in the operation.
Use the book's example campaigns as starting structures; adapt the mission path to the party's choices.
Include problems the party can address through insight, influence or other indirect action.
Give the Mystic a meaningful part in the challenge without forcing the character into the spotlight.
Let the players' inventive use of established abilities change how an obstacle is resolved.

decisionPoints: Recognize successful covert work even when the characters avoided a fight.
Choose whether XP is awarded each session or at mission completion; account for every session when an award is deferred.
Review any milestone or Motivation bonus in the context of the whole assignment.
Treat spending banked XP during a mission as an exceptional GM decision and record it explicitly.
Decide whether requested resources are temporary mission support or a lasting reward.
Consider new training or responsibilities as alternatives to public recognition.
For special equipment, decide whether it is reusable or limited to the current operation before granting it.

source.book: Edge of The Empire - Dangerous Covenants

decisionPoints: Keep XP awards grounded in the mission and the party's contribution, rather than a count of defeated enemies.
If combat dominates play, review when XP is granted and which skills are plausible to improve; revisit any temporary restriction between major fights.
When setting job pay, consider risk, location, legality, employer resources and expenses before consulting the book's pay scale.
Distinguish equipment loaned for an assignment from a lasting reward.

source.book: Age of Rebellion - Stay On Target

decisionPoints: Keep routine XP comparable with the rest of the party; consider a modest bonus for an exceptional use of Ace abilities without making it automatic each session.
Review mission complexity and the Ace's contribution instead of awarding XP simply for enemy losses.
Select suitable credits, equipment, ships, reputation, Duty or promotion rewards according to the character's affiliation and the mission outcome.

beats.prompt: Pair physical travel or a creature encounter with a choice that lets the character reflect on the bond they want to build.
Adapt the creature, habitat and other party roles to the campaign before planning the search.
Let the search, first meeting, later test and trial run respond to the party's choices; use ordinary check rules for cooperation.

decisionPoints: Use the normal XP award as the baseline; review any extra for personal goals, Motivation or Morality in light of the whole party's contributions.
Decide whether a creature or mount is temporary help or a lasting companion, and account for its care and usefulness in the campaign setting.
Treat training, talents and Force upgrades as exceptional awards with a clear eligibility and advancement decision.
For knowledge, insight or standing, record the concrete story consequence before applying any mechanical effect.
